summary: A disclosure that shows or hides one panel of content from a trigger. Three custom elements share state through context.

expanded.note: Whether the panel is shown. The trigger flips it; code can set it too.

disabled.note: Disables the trigger. The current state is kept.

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.notes: sb-collapsible: light-DOM wrapper that owns the expanded state and shares it with its parts through context. It has no shadow content of its own.

default.notes: One trigger and one content, in that order. Other markup (a heading, an always-visible item) may sit around them.

sb-toggle.note: Fires on the sb-collapsible host after expanded changes, from the trigger or from code (like <details> toggle, but it bubbles; shaped like Dialog's sb-toggle). Read host.expanded for the new state.

open.note: Content height animates from 0 to its natural height.

accessibility.role: button (the trigger); the content has no role
accessibility.accessibleNameSource: Trigger text. Host aria-label on sb-collapsible-trigger is forwarded to the inner button (ID references do not cross shadow roots, SB-0009).

keyboard.Tab: move focus to the trigger and past it; closed content is out of the tab order

aria: trigger button: aria-controls points to the sb-collapsible-content host through the ariaControlsElements property, which resolves from a shadow root to an element in the light DOM above it (Chromium exposes it in the accessibility tree only when the target has an accessibility node, and the plain content host has none); with no support for the property, aria-controls is omitted and aria-expanded still carries the state
closed content is visibility:hidden after the animation, so it is neither focusable nor read
aria-controls is re-resolved when content is added or removed after the trigger

elements.summary: The control that toggles its collapsible. Renders a native button around its slotted content.

default.notes: Text and decorative icons only; the trigger is already a button, so do not nest another control.

click.note: Pointer, Enter or Space; toggles the collapsible.

elements.notes: Must be a descendant of sb-collapsible.

elements.summary: The panel that is shown or hidden. Its height animates.

anatomy.name: content
anatomy.notes: Grid wrapper whose row animates between 0fr and 1fr.

anatomy.name: inner
anatomy.notes: Clips the content while it animates.

elements.notes: Must be a descendant of sb-collapsible.

useCases.when: One section of optional detail that a person can reveal
useCases.use: sb-collapsible with a trigger and content

useCases.when: Several related sections where one open at a time helps

antiPatterns.pattern: A button or link inside sb-collapsible-trigger
antiPatterns.why: Nested interactive controls break keyboard and screen reader use
antiPatterns.alternative: Put only text and icons in the trigger

antiPatterns.pattern: Hiding content that people must read to finish a task
antiPatterns.why: Required information behind a click is easy to miss
antiPatterns.alternative: Show it, or use Accordion only for optional detail

coverage: native button trigger named by forwarded aria-label
sb-toggle event bubbles, composed, also for programmatic changes
disabled: native disabled, no toggle, dimmed
ariaControlsElements resolves to the content host
closed content out of the tab order
focus ring keyboard-only in token color
height transition from motion token; none under reduced motion
content added after the trigger is wired (aria-controls)

drift.realization: the visual reference leaves the trigger unstyled; the ring is added so the trigger meets WCAG 2.4.7 and 1.4.11
set through the ariaControlsElements property; Chromium lists it in the accessibility tree only when the target has an accessibility node

coverage: Collapsible: 6 variant(s), State (Rest, Focus) x Open (False, True) x Disabled (False, True); read back ok

openQuestions.question: aria-controls across shadow roots: how?
openQuestions.answer: Set ariaControlsElements on the inner button (inside to outside references resolve); document that without browser support only aria-expanded remains.

openQuestions.question: Which events does the root fire?
openQuestions.answer: toggle (bubbles, composed) after every change of open, like <details>.

openQuestions.question: Is the content a region landmark?
openQuestions.answer: No: the WAI-ARIA disclosure pattern needs no role, and many collapsibles on a page would add landmark noise.
